key_insight: A linear eddy-viscosity closure can regularize the chaotic backward-time adjoint in wall turbulence, enabling the mean domain of dependence of a wall-stress sensor to be predicted and revealing two universal sensitivity structures across Reynolds numbers.
engineering_relevance: This improves our ability to infer earlier near-wall flow events from surface measurements, which is important for flow control, sensing, and state estimation in turbulent wall-bounded flows.
method: Solve the adjoint Navier–Stokes equations backward in time from a wall-stress measurement kernel.
Add a linear eddy-viscosity closure to the ensemble-averaged adjoint equations to suppress adjoint chaos.
Compare the predicted mean domain of dependence with ensemble-averaged adjoint realizations and with the domain of influence from forward perturbations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that ensemble adjoint energy grows exponentially backward in time in individual realizations, but the closure-based mean prediction matches the ensemble average and reveals Reynolds-number-universal DOD/DOI behavior.
watch_item: The closure is applied to the ensemble-averaged adjoint, so it may not capture full realization-level chaotic variability or all nonlinear near-wall sensitivity details.
paper_title: Mitigating adjoint chaos in wall turbulence
